sources_considered.why: Reports comparisons against reinforcement learning without tools using the same base-model family.
Reports improvements from prompting an existing reasoning model to invoke Python, as well as subsequent tool-focused training.
Confirms that a model explicitly implicated by the post was trained to use tools.

evidence_items.publisher: Xuefeng Li, Haoyang Zou, and Pengfei Liu / arXiv

receipt.public_excerpt: ToRL consistently outperforms baseline models across all tested benchmarks.

evidence_items.explanation: The study compares tool-integrated reinforcement learning with a baseline without tools using Qwen2.5-Math base models. It reports 43.3% AIME24 accuracy for ToRL-7B and an advantage over the tool-free baseline, supporting gains from the combined approach on mathematical tasks.

The authors activate Python tool use in the existing QwQ model through inference-time hints and report gains across their tested benchmarks. This preserves the model weights, although prompting and inference effort also change.

evidence_items.explanation: The announcement confirms contemporary pursuit of tool-using models and identifies code interpretation and web browsing. This passage establishes implementation, not a controlled performance advantage.

unresolved_gaps: These comparisons do not establish superiority across all tasks or a universal advantage at equal total compute.
They do not settle which technical definition of neurosymbolic AI the field should adopt.
